macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rebound as AI optimism returns
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.3%, the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.6%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 0.5%. Technology and semiconductor shares led the rally as strong AI-related developments eased concerns about an AI-sector slowdown.[1]

items.title: CoreWeave earnings lift AI and chip stocks
items.summary: CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion and raised its full-year revenue forecast to $13.0 billion-$13.3 billion. Its shares rose more than 24%, while semiconductor and AI-infrastructure stocks rallied broadly.[3]

items.title: Hot inflation and hawkish Fed signals boost rate-hike expectations
items.summary: A stronger-than-expected inflation report and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials increased expectations for further tightening, including a fully priced quarter-point December hike and a perceived risk of a larger move. The dollar rose to a 19-month high.[6][9]

items.title: Oil rises as U.S.-Iran tensions cloud diplomatic prospects
items.summary: Oil prices climbed, with Brent crude recovering above $92 a barrel, after renewed regional strikes weakened expectations of a near-term diplomatic resolution between the United States and Iran.[6]

items.title: OpenAI revenue and Anthropic IPO demand reinforce AI enthusiasm
items.summary: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly reached $10 billion, while strong demand for Anthropic’s planned initial public offering further supported investor sentiment toward AI companies.[3]

items.title: SoftBank reports major quarterly loss tied to data-center investment
items.summary: SoftBank reported a quarterly loss of about $7 billion, linked partly to the costs of building U.S. data centers, though the result had a limited effect on broader risk sentiment as AI-related shares recovered.[9]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market falls as inflation, yields and ETF outflows pressure prices
items.summary: Bitcoin slipped below $74,000 and Ethereum fell to about $2,053, down roughly 1.3% and 2.8% respectively over 24 hours. The broader crypto market capitalization declined about 1.6% to $2.45 trillion as hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation, higher Treasury yields and institutional ETF outflows weighed on sentiment.

items.title: NYSE plans tokenized-securities platform using Avalanche technology
items.summary: The New York Stock Exchange plans to use an Avalanche-based, permissioned blockchain as the settlement ledger for a future platform supporting around-the-clock trading of tokenized securities. The project remains under development and requires regulatory approval, while AVAX gained about 4%.

items.title: Binance hack prompts bank security checks and executive change
items.summary: U.S. regulators contacted banks to assess possible vulnerabilities after a reported $6.3 billion Binance hack. Binance also announced that Chief Financial Officer Kaiser Ng would leave, with Justin Yek expected to succeed him.

items.title: Greece approves 10% cryptocurrency capital-gains tax
items.summary: Greece’s parliament approved a bill imposing a 10% capital-gains tax on cryptocurrency, with annual gains up to about $563 exempted. The measure is described as the country’s first detailed legal framework for taxing crypto assets.

items.title: Deutsche Bank launches digital-asset custody service
items.summary: Deutsche Bank launched a custody service for institutional and corporate clients in Europe, supporting digital assets including Bitcoin and Ether. The move reflects increasing involvement by major European banks in digital-asset infrastructure.

items.title: Polish lawmakers advance cryptocurrency-related sanctions bill
items.summary: Poland’s lower house approved a bill allowing authorities to freeze cryptocurrency and other assets under a national sanctions framework. The proposal passed 240–202 and still requires Senate consideration and presidential approval.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs record $95 million in net withdrawals
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw approximately $95 million in net outflows, led by BlackRock’s IBIT with about $78.24 million withdrawn. Selling pressure contributed to Bitcoin’s decline below $74,000.

items.title: Gram rises while major cryptocurrencies sell off
items.summary: Telegram founder Pavel Durov highlighted Gram’s relative strength during the market decline; the token gained roughly 4.5% over 24 hours and traded near $1.15. Telegram is also expanding its self-custodial wallet, which reportedly saw more than 700,000 wallets created within 48 hours.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google expands access to Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to paid developers, enterprise customers and additional consumers. The model is positioned for complex coding, cybersecurity and scientific-research tasks requiring extended reasoning and verification.

items.title: AI spending growth shows signs of slowing
items.summary: New data indicates that spending growth on leading AI services such as OpenAI and Anthropic has slowed from double-digit monthly increases to single-digit growth or flat performance in some months.

items.title: Singapore startup claims major robotics-training breakthrough
items.summary: Sapiens Technology says its method reduces robotics-model training from weeks or months to roughly 30 minutes or less than a week by training only a fraction of a model’s parameters. The company is discussing pilots with more than 30 robotics and medical firms.

items.title: MIT and Carnegie Mellon researchers develop faster robot planning approach
items.summary: Researchers introduced Workspace Models, an approach that reformulates how robotic agents compress action history to improve planning speed and enable near-millisecond decision-making.

items.title: TSMC plans AI investments in Anthropic and OpenAI
items.summary: TSMC approved an investment plan of up to $1 billion involving stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI, signaling an effort to expand its AI exposure beyond advanced-chip manufacturing.

items.title: Chinese AI labs emphasize safety controls for open-weight models
items.summary: Tencent reported filtering offensive cyber content from training data for its Hunyuan Hy4 model and evaluating biological and cyber misuse risks, reflecting broader concern over the release of increasingly capable open models.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA VI reportedly surpasses $1 billion in preorders
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI has reportedly generated more than $1 billion in preorder revenue, representing an estimated 10.31 million digital copies sold before its November 19 launch. PlayStation accounts for roughly 75% of those sales, with Xbox accounting for the remainder.

items.title: GTA VI hype drives workplace and cultural preparations
items.summary: Businesses and employers are preparing for the game’s November 19 release, with Logitech announcing a gaming-related day-off benefit for employees. The Miami Heat and Take-Two are also planning a GTA-themed sports crossover ahead of launch.

items.title: Resident Evil Requiem wins 2026 Ultimate Game of the Year
items.summary: Resident Evil Requiem won the top Ultimate Game of the Year prize at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards, narrowly beating Phantom Blade Zero in reported public voting. The game also received three additional awards, including Best Lead Performer.

items.title: GTA VI preloads reportedly begin ahead of launch
items.summary: Preloading for Grand Theft Auto VI is reportedly live on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S ahead of the November 19 release. The game will also be playable through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One, while a PC version is expected later.

items.title: GTA VI expected to create major launch-week disruption
items.summary: Employers in Australia and elsewhere are anticipating increased absences when Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week. Sony and Microsoft have reportedly described it as the most preordered game in their digital marketplaces.
